questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO?
questions.explain: The carbonyl carbon is C-1; the methyl is on C-3 — 3-methylbutanal.

questions.q: What is the hybridisation of the carbonyl carbon?
questions.explain: Three σ bonds in a plane (120°) and one π bond — sp².

questions.q: Why is the boiling point of propanal (322 K) lower than that of propan-1-ol (370 K)?
options: Propanal has a smaller molecular mass
Propanal has no intermolecular hydrogen bonding
questions.explain: The alcohol has O–H···O hydrogen bonds; the aldehyde has only dipole–dipole attraction.

questions.q: What is the name of the reaction in which toluene is converted into benzaldehyde with CrO₂Cl₂?
questions.explain: The reaction of toluene with CrO₂Cl₂ is the Etard reaction.

questions.q: What is obtained when an acyl chloride is reduced with H₂ over Pd–BaSO₄?
questions.explain: This is the Rosenmund reduction — an aldehyde.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most reactive in nucleophilic addition?
questions.explain: Least steric hindrance and greatest electrophilicity.

questions.q: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones?
options: Less steric hindrance and a more electrophilic carbon
questions.explain: A ketone has two bulky, electron-releasing groups.

questions.q: Which does NOT reduce Fehling's reagent?
questions.explain: Aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's reagent.
A compound with a CH₃CO– group gives yellow CHI₃.

questions.q: What does acetaldehyde give in the presence of dilute NaOH?
Which of the following acids is the strongest?
questions.explain: The more chlorines, the more stable the carboxylate and the lower the pKₐ.

questions.q: Why is the boiling point of a carboxylic acid higher than that of an alcohol of similar mass?
options: It forms dimers with strong hydrogen bonds
questions.explain: Two O–H···O hydrogen bonds form a dimer.

questions.q: How can a carboxylic acid be distinguished from a phenol?
questions.explain: A carboxylic acid gives CO₂ with NaHCO₃; a phenol does not.
